citation.title: Preemptive RMP-driven ELM crash suppression automated by a real-time machine-learning classifier in KSTAR
citation.authors: Shin, Giwook; Han, H.; Kim, M.; Hahn, S.-H.; Ko, W.H.; et al.

topic: Real-time LSTM classifier of L/I/H/ELM states in the KSTAR PCS that triggers preprogrammed n=1 RMP; CES Ti profiles are used only offline for comparison.
own_question: Can ML-detected L-H transitions trigger preemptive RMP so that initial ELM crashes are suppressed?
actual_method_and_evidence: The classifier inputs are D-alpha and line-averaged density, downsampled to 1 kHz. Reported inference is about 800 μs in the PCS. The classifier was validated on 448 of 533 2018-campaign H-mode shots, with about 95% accuracy. Supporting evidence is a few demonstration discharges. CES Ti profiles and pedestal slopes are compared offline. The source does not estimate or nowcast CES.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In KSTAR, real-time ML inference has been embedded in the PCS. One example is an LSTM state classifier operating at a 1 kHz control cycle.
claim_checks.qualification: This is classification of confinement state from D-alpha and density. It does not estimate temperature, does not use BES/ECEI, and does not use CES as an input or a target.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are D-alpha (20 kHz) and interferometer density (10 kHz), downsampled to 1 kHz. Targets are discrete plasma-state labels. CES is used only for post-shot Ti analysis, with profiles averaged within 30 ms.
validation_if_relevant: The validation split method and the label provenance are not specified here; they are referenced to prior work.
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat this as prior CES nowcasting or Ti estimation.
Do not cite its accuracy as relevant to our estimators.
Do not claim that the CES Ti results apply to our chord or to the 2022 campaign.
Do not infer CES report latency from this source.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most, this could serve as a brief citation showing precedent for real-time ML in the KSTAR PCS. It is not otherwise relevant to our target or our inputs.
